### On Our Behalf - Truth For Life - July 1
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-july-1-2024.html
Passage: Exodus 32:31-32
Points:
- Israel abused the gold God had provided by crafting a false god to worship.
- Modern believers remain susceptible to misusing God's gifts in pursuit of personal idols.
- Moses blamelessly identified with his guilty people and pleaded for their forgiveness at personal cost.
- Moses' intercession points forward to Jesus Christ, who was cut off so sinners could be forgiven.
- Christ's mediation frees believers from wandering after idols so they can serve God wholeheartedly.

### Forgetting Any False “Gods” - The Crosswalk Devotional - August 10
Author: Vivian Bricker
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/forgetting-any-false-gods-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Exodus 32:7-8
Points:
- Anything placed ahead of God—including career, relationships, or anxiety—functions as an idol.
- Israel's quick turn to the golden calf exposed a disobedient heart that rejected God's commandments.
- The severe judgment falling on the camp reveals how seriously God views spiritual infidelity.
- Preoccupation with worries and earthly pursuits distracts believers from knowing and honoring God.
- Believers must surrender competing priorities and turn back to God for peace and forgiveness.

### Reexamining Idolatry: The Golden Calf and False Worship
Author: Jon Pentecost
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/golden-calf-false-worship/
Passage: Exodus 32:4-5
Points:
- Idolatry consists both of worshiping false gods and of worshiping the true God in unauthorized ways.
- Aaron tried to label calf worship as a feast to Yahweh, but God deemed it an abomination.
- Sincere intentions cannot excuse worship that violates God's revealed instructions.
- Sound theology is vital to Christian living because our worship must align with how God reveals Himself.
- Israel's failure reminds believers of their own sinfulness and ongoing need for Christ's grace.
